lesson_title: Your Hand Is Holding the Whole Planet
hook_text: Pick up a handful of mud. You are holding rock, water, air and life — the four spheres of planet Earth.
clip_script: Scoop up a handful of damp soil. Rub it: grains of broken rock. That is the lithosphere, litho means stone. Squeeze it: water. That is the hydrosphere, every drop on Earth, in seas, rivers, underground and in clouds. Look at the tiny gaps: air. That is the atmosphere, mostly nitrogen, one fifth oxygen. And wriggling through it all: roots, worms, fungi, billions of bacteria, rotting leaves. That is the biosphere. Here is the twist. The biosphere is not a separate layer. It is the thin zone where rock, water and air meet. Shrink Earth to an apple and all life lives in something thinner than its skin. And the spheres are always talking. Let cattle eat all the grass on a hill, and the bare soil washes into the river and fills the dam with mud. Change one sphere, and the others feel it.
visual_style: A whiteboard hand holding a soil lump that splits into four labelled bubbles; then an apple with a hair-thin glowing skin; then a bare hillside sending brown water into a dam.
mood: Surprise at the ordinary turning into the whole planet.
pacing: Four quick reveals, a slow apple-skin moment, a firm cause-and-effect ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort any place on Earth into its four spheres.
